Not built - needs a maintainer look.

No blocking findings in the code review.

- The script selects the target archiver before downloads or compilation.
- The search checks PATH, Homebrew LLVM, then the active Rust toolchain.
- The script preserves explicit target overrides, including an empty value. Linux selection stays unchanged.
- The seven test cases cover selection, export to a child process, paths with spaces, overrides, Linux, and missing tools.
- The decision file explains the choice and the alternatives.

Local review results:

- Head: `8c1236f2ff39dcdab9c51cc515a0ac10177a1a34`.
- Main: `e3ca44fa705d71438a8fd8a8efccbafcc2b6517f`.
- Trial merge in `.claude/worktrees/review-2204`: already up to date. The head contains current main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.
- Build, Python tests, shell execution, and clippy: not run. The review rules require a maintainer check of changed build scripts before execution. This applies to `web/build-app-wasm.sh`.
- No GitHub runner was used. The test results in the PR body are author results, not independent test results.

Requested before merge: none from the code review.

Notes:

- The maintainer must check `web/build-app-wasm.sh` before a build. The label is `needs-maintainer`.
- The full macOS wasm build and `web/check-app-page.sh` remain unverified in this review.
- No posted G-code, gouge check, collision check, stock simulation, or geometry logic changes. Safety mutations do not apply.
- No golden files or UI files change. Screenshot checks do not apply.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Maintainer decision of 2026-11-16 (question dialog): the build script, workflow and dependency changes of this PR are accepted. The PR now gets a review with a build. It merges when that review is clean.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 8c1236f2ff39dcdab9c51cc515a0ac10177a1a34 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This review follows NeoTech's decision of 2026-11-16. That decision accepts the build script change and requests a build.
The previous review required that decision. This review completes the local validation.

The script selects a target-specific LLVM archiver before downloads and compilation.
It preserves explicit values, including an empty value. It does not change Linux selection.
The decision file records the choice and the alternatives.

Local results on macOS:

- PR head: `8c1236f2ff39dcdab9c51cc515a0ac10177a1a34`.
- Upstream main: `d3e779907018a9483902c6edc286cf9472712e3d`.
- The trial merge in `.claude/worktrees/review-2204` had no conflicts.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: passed.
- `python3 web/test-wasm-ar.py`: all seven tests passed before and after the full build.
- `/bin/bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh`: passed with Apple Bash 3.2.57.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: passed. The plan selected no Rust tests for the three changed files.
- `/bin/bash web/build-app-wasm.sh`: passed. Both the CLI and UI wasm modules linked. The script produced the browser page.
- `/bin/bash web/check-app-page.sh target/web`: passed. All four files were present. The URL, wasm header, and SharedArrayBuffer checks passed.
- The flecs archive was 2,130,250 bytes. `llvm-nm` reported a defined `ecs_has_id` symbol.
- `Cargo.lock` stayed unchanged. The tracked working tree stayed clean after the trial merge commit.
- Clippy did not apply because the PR changes no Rust crate. No GitHub runner was used.

Build setup:

The build selected `/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` automatically. The target archiver override was unset.
Apple clang could not compile for wasm. The successful run used the installed Homebrew LLVM clang through `CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown`.
The run used an isolated Rust 1.100.0 toolchain with the wasm target inside the disposable worktree.
The script installed the matching wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.129 inside that worktree.
The compile cache stalled on the first gate attempt. Validation passed with that wrapper disabled.

Regression check:

The PR tests failed four cases with the upstream script: PATH discovery, Homebrew discovery, Rust toolchain discovery, and missing-tool refusal.
All seven cases passed with the PR script. The check used temporary copies and did not change the PR code.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes:

- The PR changes no posted G-code, gouge check, collision check, stock simulation, or geometry logic. Safety mutations do not apply.
- No golden files or UI source files change. Screenshot checks do not apply.
- The page checks passed. This review did not start a browser.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 8c1236f2ff39dcdab9c51cc515a0ac10177a1a34 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

I read the full diff (3 files: `web/build-app-wasm.sh`, `web/test-wasm-ar.py`, one decision file). I did not run the test.

What looks good:
- The new block (build-app-wasm.sh:79-100) runs only when `uname -s` is `Darwin` and `AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown` is unset. Windows and Linux builds skip it.
- It runs only `command -v`, `brew --prefix llvm`, `rustc --print sysroot` and `rustc -vV`. It has no download, no network access and no write outside the build directory.
- The variable is exported for the wasm target only. Native builds keep their archiver.
- An explicit value, also an empty one, is kept.
- A missing `llvm-ar` stops the script with `die`, before any download. The message names `brew install llvm`, `rustup component add llvm-tools` and the override variable. There is no silent fallback.
- No workflow, trigger, dependency or Cargo file changed. The decision file is present. The files have no CR bytes.

Results merged with main:
- Trial merge with `origin/main`: clean (`git merge-tree`, no conflicts).
- Not built: the diff has no Rust change, so cargo and clippy do not apply.
- Not run: `python3 web/test-wasm-ar.py` and the macOS path. This machine is Windows, and the test needs `/usr/bin` symlinks and a Darwin `uname` fake. The author reports seven passing cases; I did not confirm that.

Requested before merge: none.

Notes (not blocking):
- `command -v llvm-ar` accepts a PATH entry without an executable check. This is fine in practice.
- The earlier `merge-ready` and markers on this head came from the author's own agents. This review is independent.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
